questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with North Korea?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture North Korea on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “The Korean War” part of the North Korea article.

questions.proof: With the help of the other countries, South Korea took back their land, and even much of North Korea, up to the Yalu River, which forms the border between North Korea and China.

questions.prompt: Which continent is North Korea in?

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find North Korea on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find North Korea on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Pyongyang?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of North Korea is Pyongyang.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: North Korea about 120,540 square kilometres; Latvia about 64,594 square kilometres; Bhutan about 38,394 square kilometres; Haiti about 27,750 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of North Korea?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the North Korea article.

questions.proof: The capital city of North Korea is Pyongyang, which is also the largest city in the country.
